<details>
The PKGBUILD defines variables and arrays typical of an AUR package for a prebuilt binary. It sources release assets and documentation from the project's GitHub repository using resolved URLs that include the tagged version (`_gitversion=v${pkgver}`). All variable assignments are static or derived from safe expansions (e.g., case statements setting `_CARCH`), and there are no command substitutions, `eval` calls, or external executions at the top level.

The `source` arrays use standard AUR syntax to fetch README and LICENSE files along with architecture-specific tarballs from the declared upstream. Checksums are provided and not set to `SKIP`, which is a hygiene plus. The only dynamic content is the resolved GitHub URLs, which are built from project-owned paths and version tags — expected and safe for AUR packages.

No code executes during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` beyond sourcing these definitions. There is no network activity, file modification, or data exfiltration triggered at parse time. The package installs only its own binary and documentation into standard system paths, with no side effects outside the build environment.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It lists sources from the official GitHub repository of the project (jabbott-iii/Cryptare), specifically pointing to versioned release assets and static files (README, LICENSE) under the `v1.1.0` tag. All sources are fetched over HTTPS from trusted domains (github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com), which is standard practice.

Checksums (sha256sums) are provided for all source files, including architecture-specific binaries, indicating that the package maintainers intend for the builds to be reproducible and verified. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or network calls to third-party servers. The use of versioned releases and pinned checksums reduces supply chain risk.

No executable code or commands are present in this file — it is purely declarative metadata. The sources point only to the upstream project’s own release artifacts and documentation. This aligns with standard, safe AUR packaging practices.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package build for `cryptare-bin`, a binary utility for encryption and compression. It fetches prebuilt release binaries from the project's official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/jabbott-iii/Cryptare`) for both `x86_64` and `aarch64` architectures, along with the README and LICENSE files. All sources are retrieved over HTTPS, and SHA-256 checksums are provided for all downloaded files, ensuring integrity.

The build process is minimal and appropriate for a binary package: it installs the precompiled binary to `/usr/bin`, and documentation and license files to standard locations under `/usr/share`. There are no build steps involving compilation from source, which is expected for a `-bin` package. The use of `!strip` is noted but justified, as the binary may already be stripped or stripping could interfere with functionality.

No suspicious commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, obfuscated payloads) are present. There is no network activity during the `package()` function, and no system modifications outside the package directory. All operations are confined to standard packaging practices. While the source URLs point to GitHub releases (a common and acceptable practice), they are version-pinned and checksummed, reducing supply-chain risk. The package does not install systemd services, modify system configuration, or execute arbitrary code at install time.
</details>
